nodes.name: Thomas E. Dewey
nodes.note: Thomas E. Dewey (1902–1971), governor of New York and Republican nominee for president in 1944 and 1948. On 15 October 1944, after meeting Abba Hillel Silver, he declared for 'a free and democratic Jewish Commonwealth' in Palestine with unrestricted immigration; on 7 October 1946 he called for immigration of 'not 100,000, but of several hundreds of thousands'.

nodes.name: Republican platform, Palestine plank (1944)
nodes.note: Adopted 26 June 1944: called for opening Palestine to unrestricted Jewish immigration and land ownership under the Balfour Declaration and the Mandate, and condemned 'the failure of the President to insist' that Britain honour them.

nodes.name: Roosevelt's heart failure, concealed (1944)
nodes.note: On 28 March 1944 the cardiologist Howard Bruenn found Roosevelt in acute congestive heart failure. On 10 July 1944 Frank Lahey wrote that over another term 'he would again have heart failure and be unable to complete it'. The memo was suppressed for wartime security and published decades later; Roosevelt ran for a fourth term and died on 12 April 1945.
